lines.trans: What is this phony-looking video?
You're originally from Fukushima, aren't you?
Huh? How did you know?
From your dialect. I'm from Fukushima too.
What a coincidence! Herring pickled with pepper leaves—brings back memories, doesn't it?
Then maybe I'll join you for a drink as a fellow hometown native.
Well then, cheers to two lonely souls.
It's been ages since I drank this much. You really hold your liquor well.
Did your husband work for the national railway?
Yes. He used to sell boxed lunches at Sapporo Station.
You were awake, huh? This footage is truly wonderful.
Thank you.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.

examples.text: いや、方言。俺も福島です。
examples.trans: From your dialect. I'm from Fukushima too.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: それじゃ、さみしんぼうさん二人に乾杯。
examples.trans: Well then, cheers to two lonely souls.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。
そう。札幌駅で弁当売りやってたの。

meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.en: to happen; to occur; to wake up
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.trans: I wake up at seven every morning.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
